overall_summary: Analysis of 47 unique Shorts reveals extreme exoplanet mysteries and visceral first-person hypothetical survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') consistently drive the highest views (800–1,050+) and engagement (likes >35, comments). In contrast, generic psychology brain facts and repeated re-uploads of space silence/memory topics severely underperform (<50 views, 0 engagement). Story-first immersion and extreme physical environments dominate channel traction.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Extreme Space Survival ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) deliver 5x-10x channel average views and top engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Produce cinematic first-person hypothetical journeys into extreme, lethal astronomical or planetary phenomena.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,031 views, 36 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views, 25 likes) outperform typical science trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on high-contrast, paradoxical planetary environments highlighting tangible sensory extremes (temperatures, atmospheric pressure, visual darkness).

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple iterations of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5–53 views, 0 likes) and earworm trivia (17–71 views) consistently fail to gain algorithmic traction.
weak_patterns.action: Retire abstract cognitive psychology factoids in favor of narrative-driven mystery, cinematic survival, or shocking historical anomalies.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' re-uploads plateaued at 34–220 views with minimal interaction.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid passive explanatory hooks; frame topics around danger, visual drama, or counter-intuitive paradoxes.
